summary: I sent the exact brief. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and read NOTES.md, the activity page source and the four UI guideline files. Then an auto-compaction happened (two compact_boundary entries), and the skill was restored afterwards. Next the agent said the task was bounded and that the design would stay in chat. It ran scripts/start-server.sh, wrote filter-placement.html with three layouts (A: filter bar above the table, B: quick-filter chips, C: a Filter button with a popover), gave me a localhost URL with a ?key= value, and asked me to reply in the terminal. I picked A. The agent wrote a waiting.html screen and asked a non-visual question in the terminal about which filters to include (I chose to add a date range). It then gave a full design in chat and asked "Does this look right? I'll start once you say yes." I said yes. It started implementation work: it ran shell commands, then asked about how the CSS should handle design tokens. No spec file and no plan document were created.
reasoning: All 8 criteria were met, and the session log and files on disk back each one. The companion opened just-in-time after an auto-compaction landed between loading the skill and the first visual question, which is exactly the situation this scenario targets. The task stayed bounded: the design stayed in chat, and no spec or plan was written. The agent asked for approval before coding and started implementing after I said yes.

observations.description: The first launch exited by accident. After the 'Newer Opus model available' prompt, the Bypass Permissions warning came up with 'No, exit' selected by default, and a single Enter closed Claude Code. The workspace trust prompt also defaults to 'No, exit'. I had to relaunch.

At startup a 'Newer Opus model available' dialog said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. The banner then showed Opus 5.5, so the dialog's 'pinned' value looks wrong.

The log has two compact_boundary entries about 52 seconds apart (23:42:00 and 23:42:52), both during the opening reading phase. The screen showed '0% until auto-compact' and 'Compacting conversation…' for about 46s. After compaction the skill came back ('Skills restored (hyperpowers:brainstorming)') and the agent re-read SKILL.md.

The companion message warned that 'The browser tab uses a lot of tokens' and offered to stay in the terminal. That is fair, but it adds friction. It also suggested adding .hyperpowers/ to a .gitignore, which is helpful.

After approval the agent stopped to ask how the CSS should handle tokens, because the shared token sheet named in the guidelines isn't in the repo. That is a reasonable question, but it shows the fixture's guideline docs point to a file that doesn't exist.

The agent offered A as its recommendation in the terminal while showing the options in the browser. That is good guidance, but it means a terminal-only user could choose without looking at the sketches.

The agent asked nothing before this. Its message said "The first question is where the filters go, and that's easier to see than to describe." After my pick, it asked "What should the activity filter bar filter on?" as an AskUserQuestion in the terminal, and the browser only showed a waiting.html screen ("Continuing in terminal...").

Screen: "I'd treat this as a bounded change: it filters a table that already exists in public/activity.html, so I'll put a short design here in chat instead of writing a spec." The final design was given in chat.
`ls docs` shows only ui-guidelines. There is no docs/superpowers or docs/hyperpowers directory. `git status --short` shows only `?? .hyperpowers/` (the companion's screens).

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: Counting `"skill":` in the session log gives one entry: hyperpowers:brainstorming. No writing-plans Skill call was made, and git status shows no plan file.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of the layout before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: The companion message asked me to "Click one in the browser if you like, then reply here." Later the agent asked "Does this look right? I'll start once you say yes." No edits to public/ happened before that: git status was clean apart from .hyperpowers/.

After my "Yes, looks good — go ahead." the screen showed "Ran 4 shell commands" and then "HTML/JS are settled, but CSS hits a snag...". The agent then asked a follow-up question about tokens in activity.css, so implementation was under way.
